zed.note: System libraries from its script/linux; on macOS its shaders build with Xcode's Metal compiler. `--help` is answered before a window opens. Its tests are those of the crates below gpui: the rest run on gpui's headless test platform, but the whole suite with dev and release builds is longer than a hosted runner's six hours.

servo.note: v0.7.0. System libraries from its python/servo/platform (apt_common.txt, apt_ubuntu_only.txt, Brewfile); SpiderMonkey is mozjs's prebuilt archive. Its tests are those of crates without a window or a GPU.

bun.note: bun's Rust port (bun-v1.4.3). bunprep.py builds its C and C++ once (in `nix develop .#bench-bun`, which has what that needs) and adds the member bun-exe, whose link takes them.

dynamo.note: NVIDIA Dynamo v1.6.1, as its AGENTS.md builds it, on runners without a GPU: the workspace (`cargo build`; on macOS dynamo-llm without its Linux-only default feature), and the Python bindings, a workspace of their own that maturin builds with cargo, imported. CUDA is loaded at run time (cudarc's fallback-latest) and nixl-sys builds its stubs without NIXL, so the default features build. The build scripts need protoc and libclang (bindgen). The program run is the CPU-only vLLM mocker server.

codex.note: OpenAI's Codex CLI, rust-v0.165.0: its Rust workspace is codex-rs, pinned to Rust 1.99.1 (rust-toolchain.toml), which bench.py's cargo builds with. System libraries from its rust-ci-full.yml (libcap for the Linux sandbox, ALSA for voice) and OpenSSL, which hosted runners have. The v8 crate's build script downloads its prebuilt static library, which `blaze lock --fetches` records first (`fetches`). `--version` needs no API key or network. Its tests are the unit and integration tests of crates that need neither a model, a network nor credentials.
